Okay, I just started practicing this so take it for what it's worth, but it's helping me so I'll throw it out there.

I think the biggest mistake I've been making when relapsing is that I don't stop the thoughts or derail the urges IMMEDIATELY.

Since I'm personally addicted to pr0n, usually a picture or a memory of a favorite clip will pop up and I more or less subconsciously allow it to linger, and if I let myself think about that image even for a few seconds it takes hold and gets my adrenaline/hormones pumping and then pretty soon I'm off to the computer.

So I've been super vigilant about shutting down those images/thoughts the split second they appear. In fact I've been "switching" the thoughts to remembrances of times I was really miserable or ashamed as a result of acting out in the past.

I'm doing the second part because that's how I quit drinking years ago. Whenever I had the desire for a drink, I would force myself to remember the worst time I had because of drinking (my bottom). It took 2 or 3 months of effort, but the upside is that eventually the thoughts/desires went away completely and I've never seriously wanted a drink since - and haven't had one in 25 years. it's a form of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.

Anyway, I'm having gppd luck with it after being on a miserable relapse and with any luck maybe it will help someone else.
Objectifying thoughts works for me. "Am I actually horny, or are pixels activating my reward circuitry?" "Do I want to fap? Or do I just want release?"
